# PR-head provisioning narration: acme/widget#82, N=1

**Aliases.**
- `ROOT=/work/widget`
- `W=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` (`<name>` is `fix/retry` with `/` replaced by `-`)
- `H=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- `B=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`
- `C=cccc…` (40 chars)
- `D=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`

The caller passed PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1.

## Shared discovery (every row)

| # | cwd | Command / resolution | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| d1 | session cwd | `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` | `GIT_COMMON=/work/widget/.git`, so ROOT = `/work/widget` |
| d2 | session cwd | `git -C ROOT rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` | empty, so not a submodule |
| d3 | — | Overrides ladder under ROOT | None exist (except in **override**), so legacy path; no native tool or wrapper, so home is W |
| d4 | — | Fetch | `git -C ROOT fetch origin` |
| d5 | — | Head verify | `git -C ROOT rev-parse --verify -q H^{commit}` passes; `git -C ROOT rev-parse origin/fix/retry` = H |
| d6 | — | Base resolve | `BASE_SHA=$(git -C ROOT rev-parse origin/main)` = B |
| d7 | — | Ordered stops | Fork check, then `git -C ROOT worktree list --porcelain` (no fix/retry), then local branch (absent) |

**Pre-write boundary:** nothing at d1–d7 creates or modifies a file or runs `worktree add`.

## Success legend (S)

| # | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| s1 | `git -C ROOT status --porcelain` | Exit 0, empty, so clean |
| s2 | `git -C ROOT check-ignore -q .worktrees` | Exit 0, already ignored, so no commit |
| s3 | `git -C ROOT worktree add W fix/retry` | No caller `-b`. Git's unique-remote DWIM resolves it as `--track -b fix/retry W origin/fix/retry`. |
| s4 | `git -C ROOT worktree list --porcelain` | Lists `worktree W` |
| s5 | `git -C W rev-parse HEAD` | = H |
| s6 | Capture | `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=H`, `BASE_SHA=B` |
| s7 | `git -C W merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` | Base already an ancestor: `merge: no-op - head contains origin/main`, no commit |
| s8 | `git -C W merge-base --is-ancestor H HEAD` | Exit 0 |
| s9 | `git -C ROOT symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` | Empty output, so the provenance note is skipped |

**Report R:**
```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#82
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
Base SHA: bbbbbbb
merge: no-op - head contains origin/main
Ready to implement PR #82 rework
```

## Provisioning rows

| Row | Delta from legends |
|---|---|
| **linked** | d1 runs in `/work/widget/.worktrees/other`. `GIT_DIR=/work/widget/.git/worktrees/other` ≠ common dir, but ROOT is still `/work/widget`. `other` is not the selected home on fix/retry, so it is not adopted and nothing is nested inside it. Run S with s1 in ROOT, then R. |
| **primary** | d1 gives GIT_DIR == common dir. Otherwise S, then R. |
| **ancestor** | d7 finds local `fix/retry`=C. `git -C ROOT merge-base --is-ancestor fix/retry origin/fix/retry` exits 0. After s1/s2, run `git -C ROOT update-ref refs/heads/fix/retry origin/fix/retry` (never `branch -f`). Then `git -C ROOT worktree add W fix/retry` checks out the existing branch, with no DWIM and no `-b`. Then s4–s9, then R. |
| **reuse** | d7 lists W on fix/retry, which is the selected home and not a collision; ancestry exits 0. Run `git -C W status --porcelain` (clean, no ask). Run `git -C W merge --ff-only origin/fix/retry`; s5 gives ccccccc → H. No `worktree add`, no s2/s3/s9. Then s6–s8, then R. |
| **fork** | Stop: `PR #82's head lives on fork contributor/widget; rework needs an in-repo branch.` Boundary: after d6, before s1. |
| **elsewhere** | Stop: `branch fix/retry is checked out at /work/widget/.worktrees/pr-82; finish or remove that worktree first.` Boundary: after d7's list, before s1. |
| **unreachable** | d5's verify fails. Stop: `PR #82 head aaaaaaa is not reachable (origin/fix/retry is at ddddddd); the branch moved.` Boundary: after fetch, before s1. |
| **moved** | d5 finds `origin/fix/retry`=ddddddd ≠ H. Same stop text as **unreachable**, same boundary. |
| **ahead / diverged** | Each run: local fix/retry = ccccccc, ancestry exits 1. Stop: `local branch fix/retry is at ccccccc, not an ancestor of origin/fix/retry (aaaaaaa); rework needs the PR head.` Boundary: before s1, so no `update-ref` and no add. |
| **override** | d3 reads `## using-git-worktrees` with `create:` containing `-b`, so the override is skipped and home stays the default W. Run s1–s9 with the built-in s3. R gains `create: override skipped (contains -b)` after the merge line. |
| **race** | s1–s4 succeed; s5 returns D. Stop: `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry is at dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd, not PR #82 head aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa; left intact.` No reset or removal. Writes were s3 only. No s6–s8 and no R. |

## History (successful rows)

- **Merge forward only.** Every commit reachable from `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=H` is preserved.
- **Forbidden:** no `rebase`, and no `reset` or `commit --amend` on any commit at or below H. Keeping the tree current means merging `origin/main` again, never rebasing.
- **Still allowed:** the flow's spec-approval `commit --amend --no-edit`, which only touches the spec commit above H.
- **Still allowed:** the appended-wave fold `reset --soft "$WAVE_BASE_SHA"`, provided `WAVE_BASE_SHA` descends from H.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: both outputs already route through reference/pr-head.md ahead of linked reuse, select W without adopting or nesting under `other`, use `worktree add W fix/retry` with DWIM explicitly distinguished from caller `-b`, do ancestry-then-update-ref (no `branch -f`), check dirt before `--ff-only`, emit every stop with the exact one-line text before any write, skip the `-b` override with the required line, leave the raced tree intact, and keep merge-forward history with the amend and `reset --soft` carve-outs. After actually tightens the report fact slightly by dropping Before's `(clean)` suffix so `Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa` is the literal line, and it adds an explicit pre-write boundary and `check-ignore` step, which is fine. Two small things to watch so future rows don't regress: After abbreviates alias C as `cccc…` while the brief asks for full-SHA aliases defined once (the row text uses `ccccccc`, so the stop lines still name the SHA), and the race stop wording was reworded (`is at ... not PR #82 head ...; left intact`) — keep it naming home and both full SHAs as it does now, and keep the `Writes were s3 only` / `No reset or removal` note. Since the Expected-to-move entries for routing and history were already satisfied by Before's text, the Change is delivered without cost; if you extend this wording to keyed multi-member legs, carry the same per-row `cwd`/`-C ROOT` and `-C W` targeting so the selected-worktree facts stay explicit.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Nothing moved: every fact holds in both outputs, so the After wording preserved the single-member provisioning facts but did not visibly deliver the intended routing shift — neither Before nor After names reference/pr-head.md or shows a Step 0 hook that selects the PR-head owner before linked reuse; both just assert 'selected home resolves to W / not the unrelated session tree' inside discovery, which Before already did. If you want pr-head/routing to be a genuine fails→holds, add an explicit discovery sentence such as 'Resolved PR values route through reference/pr-head.md first; generic linked-worktree reuse of other is considered only if no PR head is supplied', and keep the ROOT/BRANCH keyed-leg statement separate so primary/linked rows still show W on fix/retry. Two After edits are worth tightening so they do not drift later: the race stop dropped 'the PR head changed during provisioning' and the 'expected' phrasing (still names home and both full SHAs, so it holds, but keep the reference's exact line), and the history row's 'never ... replace commits at/below A using reset or amend' sits awkwardly beside the permitted amend/reset --soft clause — phrase it as 'never rewrite commits reachable from A; the appended-spec amend and appended-wave reset --soft of commits above A remain allowed' to avoid an apparent self-contradiction.
